note.question: How can online retailing be represented using feature-based consideration set choice?
note.overview: The paper proposes a feature-based consideration set choice model (FCM) motivated by customers’ purchasing behavior in online retail platforms. In our model, customers form a consideration set by including products with the highest utilities computed based on a subset of product features visible on the search results page. The customers then make a purchase decision from the consideration set by accounting for all features available on the product pages.

source.section: D-FCM: Deterministic Assumption on Consideration Utilities
source.quote: We refer to this variant as the deter­ ministic feature-based consideration set choice model, which is formally defined next.

Our model differs from the TMNL model in three ways. (1) We allow product utilities to evolve from the consider­ ation to the purchase stage, (2) we capture heterogene­ ity in customer preferences in the purchase stage, and (3) the consideration set is formed based on the real­ ized (consideration) utilities.

A widely popular class of discrete choice mod­ els is the random utility maximization (RUM) model (McFadden 1981), which assumes that customers associate a utility with each product, consisting of a deterministic component and a stochastic (random) component.

On the positive side, the D-FCM admits a tractable mixed integer linear programming (MILP) formulation for solving the assortment problem and facilitates the study of the more complex joint assortment and pricing problem, for which we provide a polynomial-time solution (in the number of products) for both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.
Methodology/results: We develop an efficient maximum likelihood estimation procedure for estimating the model parameters from customers’ click and purchase data.
